item.title: Toluwanisings laid to rest in Ibadan
item.description: By Wasiu Rokibat Nigerian gospel singer Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, has been laid to rest at his residence in Ibadan, Oyo State, bringing an end to weeks of disagreement among members of his family over his final resting place. The gospel artiste was buried on Monday, November 9, 2026, in a private ceremony attended by family members following a funeral service at Banjola Event and Conference Centre, Alakia, Ibadan. His burial came after a disagreement between his widow, Olayemi Elizabeth Damilola, and his paternal relatives over where his remains should be interred. While his paternal family had expressed concerns about the circumstances surrounding his death and initially pushed for his burial in Ikirun, Osun State, his widow and associates were involved in discussions over the final arrangements. The disagreement attracted public attention and eventually prompted the intervention of the Oyo State Police Command. On November 3, the parties involved signed a peace undertaking at the police command headquarters in Eleyele, Ibadan, agreeing to avoid further public exchanges and actions capable of escalating tensions. Speaking on the agreement, the police command stated that, “All parties agreed to maintain peace and be of good behaviour, refrain from any act capable of causing a breach of the peace.” The intervention paved the way for the family to settle on burying the singer at his Ibadan residence, where his wife and children live. Toluwanisings, who was widely recognised for his energetic worship ministrations and gospel songs, including A Very Big God, died on October 14, 2026. His death generated reactions across the gospel music community, while the disagreement surrounding his burial further drew public attention to the family’s situation. item.title: 2027 will test clarity of Nigeria’s legal framework on electoral justice – INEC
item.description: …warns AI, digital threats may spill into courtrooms … as 375 tribunal judges take oath By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) on Monday said the 2027 general elections would test not only its operational preparedness but also the effectiveness and clarity of the nation’s legal framework for electoral justice. According to the Commission, the political stability of the nation will depend not only on how efficiently it conducts elections, but equally on how courageously, transparently and justly the judiciary adjudicates the disputes that follow. The Chairman of the electoral body, Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, spoke at the opening ceremony of a three-day workshop for Justices of the Court of Appeal and members of the 2027 election petition tribunals held at the Body of Benchers Complex in Abuja. The workshop was preceded by the inauguration of 375 judges who will serve on tribunals that will hear election petitions filed by aggrieved parties across the country. Section 285(1) and (2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, vests in the President of the Court of Appeal the responsibility of constituting Election Petition Tribunals for the adjudication of disputes arising from National and State Houses of Assembly and Governorship elections. Similarly, Section 134(3)(a) and (b) of the Electoral Act, 2026, prescribes the timelines for constituting the tribunals and opening their registries. Describing the workshop’s theme, “Election Tribunal as a Tool for Political Stability,” as apt, the INEC Chairman stressed that, with the general election scheduled to commence on January 16, 2027, the Commission recognises that the legitimacy of the country’s constitutional democracy rests upon impartial electoral administration and fearless judicial adjudication. He said: “While INEC manages the ballot, deploys technology, and safeguards the voter franchise, the Election Petition Tribunals stand as the ultimate guardians of democratic legitimacy. “When political contestations overflow from polling units into the courtroom, the Judiciary provides the constitutional sanctuary where grievances are transformed into peace, unlawful shortcuts are corrected, and the sovereign choice of the electorate is vindicated under the Rule of Law. “The credibility of elections cannot be measured solely by the conduct of voting or the declaration of results. It depends equally on public confidence that electoral disputes will be determined independently, fairly and in accordance with the law. “Citizens must be assured not only that their votes count, but also that the legal system is capable of protecting their democratic choices. “The consequences of electoral judgments frequently extend beyond candidates and political parties. They affect public confidence, the legitimacy of elected institutions and democratic stability. “Judicial scrutiny also provides an important mechanism of accountability for election administration. item.title: Pat Utomi blasts Tinubu’s govt, asks what Nigerians pay taxes for
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Political economist Pat Utomi has accused the APC-led government of abandoning its responsibilities while Nigerians pay out of pocket for basic services, from electricity and water to roads, healthcare and education. In a post on his X handle on Monday, Utomi questioned what citizens receive in return for paying taxes when households and communities must fund services that government is expected to provide. “The only thing this APC-led government is good at doing is making your life worse,” he wrote. Utomi said Nigerians buy generators to cope with unreliable electricity, sink boreholes for water and contribute money to repair roads. He also cited private security, healthcare and schools as costs families increasingly bear because public institutions have been neglected. He added that waste disposal, drainage, streetlights and transformers had also become private financial responsibilities. “Then what exactly are we paying this APC-led government to do?” he asked, arguing that governments elsewhere invest public resources in education, healthcare, infrastructure and social welfare. Utomi also criticised the government’s appeals for patience and sacrifice amid economic hardship. He cited the removal of petrol subsidies and increases in electricity tariffs and university fees, alongside rising healthcare costs. “But how much more must the people sacrifice while those in power continue to enjoy the privileges of office?” he asked. Utomi argued that taxation obliges government to provide public services, describing it as more than a contribution from citizens to politicians. “The government cannot collect from the people, abandon its responsibilities and then demand applause from the people they’re making their lives difficult,” he wrote. He concluded with a challenge to the government: “If Nigerians must finance their own survival, what exactly is the purpose of government?” In a separate post on Sunday, Utomi said the APC government had made the daily struggle to earn a living an unbearable burden for hardworking Nigerians. He described the hardship as a tragedy for a richly endowed nation that he believes is poorly governed. He said: “The incompetence of the APC government has turned the daily struggle for survival into an unbearable burden for hardworking Nigerians. Those who labour honestly to earn a living are being punished by a system that should be making their lives easier. What a tragedy for a nation so richly endowed yet so poorly governed!” The post Pat Utomi blasts Tinubu’s govt, asks what Nigerians pay taxes for appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: PDP, ADC, SDP chieftains defect to APC in Ondo
item.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure Chieftains of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), African Democratic Congress (ADC) and Social Democratic Party (SDP) in Igbara-Oke, Ifedore Local Government Area of Ondo State, have defected to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) ahead of the 2027 general elections. The defectors were received by an APC delegation led by Senator Niyi Adegbonmire, representing Ondo Central Senatorial District, and Hon. Festus Akingbaso, member of the House of Representatives, alongside other party leaders. Speaking on behalf of the defectors, Bayo Adejuwon said their decision to join the APC was motivated by what he described as the developmental strides of the ruling party in the area. Adejuwon said the APC leadership was familiar with their political influence, adding that their contributions would be reflected in the party’s performance in the 2027 elections. He said the new members were committed to working for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and the victory of other APC candidates in the state. Another defector, Faloyo, who identified himself as an indigene of Ijare, expressed satisfaction with the decision to join the APC and pledged to mobilise votes from his community for Tinubu and other party candidates in the January 16 and February 6 elections. Addressing the gathering, former Ondo State APC Chairman, Engr. Ade Adetimehin, described the defectors as the last batch of PDP members in the ward. He said their defection demonstrated the APC’s growing presence in the area and urged them to return to their respective communities to begin mobilisation ahead of the elections. Adetimehin expressed confidence in the electoral prospects of Tinubu, Adegbonmire and Akingbaso, describing the APC as an inclusive party. Also speaking, an APC leader in Ifedore, Tobi Ogunleye, said the defection was voluntary, insisting that the new members were not recruited through inducement. He alleged that some APC members in the state were working against the interests of the party’s candidates under the guise of a Rainbow Coalition, insisting that those at the gathering represented the authentic APC. Ogunleye warned that anyone working against the party’s candidates was undermining Tinubu’s transformation agenda. He also attributed the weakening of the ADC and SDP in the state to the influence of the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo. Ogunleye further claimed that the defection had effectively eliminated opposition presence in Ifedore, describing the new APC members as key figures in the opposition political structure before their decision to join the ruling party. item.title: British Comedian Russell Brand Jailed 10 Years For Rape, Assault
item.description: British comedian and TV star Russell Brand was Monday jailed for more than 10 years for a string of sex offences, including rape as the judge told him he had been a “sexual predator” whose fame had protected him. Brand, 51, showed no emotion as Judge Joel Bennathan said he had acted with “staggering arrogance” and shown “contempt” for his victims who had suffered significant and lasting harm. Paying tribute to the “bravery” of the women who came forward, the judge told Brand he had acted “how you liked and when you liked, unhindered by the rules by which decent people live”. His wife Laura Gallacher, with whom he has three children, slumped in her seat in the public gallery of London’s Southwark Crown Court as the total sentence of 10 years and six months was announced. Brand told his wife, who has supported him in court throughout the case, “we’ll be OK” as he was led down to the cells. The disgraced star was convicted by a jury last week of one rape and three sexual assaults committed against four women between 2004 and 2009. Laura Gallacher (C), the wife of British comedian and actor Russell Brand is helped into a car after the sentencing of British comedian and TV star Russell Brand (Photo by HENRY NICHOLLS / AFP) The sentence marks the final fall in a scandal-hit showbiz career that saw him embody the anything-goes culture of 2000s British TV and radio. Brand, who has reinvented himself as an online Christian guru, held a string of prayer beads and made the sign of the cross before one of his victims personally read out her impact statement from behind a screen. The woman said she had been left “traumatised” by the assault in a London bar in 2004. “For many years, as his star was rising, it was impossible to escape seeing him all over the media, being celebrated for his disgusting behaviour against women like it was all a joke,” she told the court. Brand listened impassively, looking straight ahead. ‘Celebrated’ Russell Brand’s father ”Ron” Brand (L) leaves the court building after the sentencing of British comedian and TV star Russell Brand takes place at Southwark Crown Court in south London on November 9, 2026.(Photo by JUSTIN TALLIS / AFP) A second woman, a 21-year-old fan he raped in 2009 after they met at one of his shows, told the court she had felt she simply would “not be believed” if she reported him. “His fame, wealth and influence created a power imbalance which made me feel powerless,” she said, adding the consequences of the rape had “affected almost every aspect of my life”. The hearing came as Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the victims’ bravery would bring about wider changes to the legal system. Burnham pledged to be “relentless in making whatever improvements we can” to provide more support for victims, including setting up teams in every police force for handling rapes and serious sexual offences. item.title: Akwa Ibom not involved in opposition harassment – NISMA boss
item.description: By Steve Oko The Akwa Ibom State Government has denied allegations of intimidation and harassment of opposition politicians, insisting that the state provides a peaceful and inclusive political environment for all parties ahead of the 2027 general elections. The Chairman of the Nigeria Institute for Social Media Analysts (NISMA), Akwa Ibom State chapter, and Special Assistant on Media to Governor Umo Eno, Venerable Richard Peters, said the governor had consistently advocated peaceful and issue-based political engagement. Peters, who spoke with Vanguard on the sidelines of a two-day forum for journalists, NISMA members and media executives organised by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Enugu, said Eno had warned his aides against any conduct capable of promoting political violence. He was reacting to reports of alleged harassment of opposition supporters during recent political activities ahead of the 2027 elections. Peters, however, maintained that Akwa Ibom was not involved in such incidents, suggesting that reports circulating might have confused the state with a neighbouring state. “Akwa Ibom has never been in the news for any bad reason. We have a very free political ambience for all political actors. We are open to all politicians because the governor has made it so,” he said. According to him, Eno had repeatedly directed his aides to promote peace, warning that anyone unwilling to uphold the administration’s commitment to peaceful political engagement risked being sacked. “The governor has been preaching peace. Anywhere he goes, his body language is peace. He even told his aides that anybody who will not carry his message of peace will be fired. “He does not want violence and does not support abuse. His position is that political actors should go on issues. Whatever programme or initiative you have, tell the people what you intend to do and how you will do it. Don’t resort to propaganda,” Peters said. He explained that the governor’s position was aimed at ensuring that political competition in the state focused on policies, programmes and development alternatives rather than personal attacks. Commends INEC’s media engagement Peters also commended INEC for organising the media engagement, describing it as evidence of the commission’s commitment to credible elections in 2027. He said the presentations and capacity-building sessions at the forum showed that the commission was putting measures in place to deliver free, fair and credible elections. He particularly praised INEC for addressing the communication gap between the electoral body and the media, noting that limited access to official information sometimes compelled journalists to rely on unverified reports on social media. He said the engagement would strengthen professional and ethical election reporting by improving journalists’ access to credible information. item.title: Nvidia plunges but tech shares rebound, oil prices slump
item.description: Technology share prices clawed back some of last week’s sharp losses on Monday, though gains were tempered by a plunge in Nvidia following a probe into its boss Jensen Huang over claims of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Oil prices fell five percent on hopes for diplomatic talks aimed at ending the US-Iran war. Chipmakers and other companies linked to the artificial intelligence boom took a hammering in the days after last Tuesday’s US midterm elections, which saw Democrats sweep both chambers of Congress, leading to speculation lawmakers would seek to rein in tech firms. But Wall Street’s main indices opened higher, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq adding 0.9 percent. Briefing.com analyst Patrick O’Hare said the rebound in equities was due to more than just the drop in oil prices. “What we also have this morning is an inclination to buy into last week’s weakness, and specifically into the large losses seen in the AI trade,” he said in a note to clients. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, which includes major chipmakers and AI firms, rose 1.9 percent. But the gains did not extend to Nvidia, which saw its shares slump more than eight percent as trading got underway in New York. O’Hare said Nvidia was being treated as a one-off story by investors for the moment. “In other words, the stock is being penalized for Jensen Huang’s personal transgression, which has invited a great deal of uncertainty into the mix, but the market isn’t caught up in the notion that this situation is going to have a systemic domino effect,” he said. The news that Nvidia’s board would investigate whether Huang had been targeted in a foreign espionage plot, following his admission he was unfaithful to his wife, brought fresh uncertainty in the markets. The New York Times last month reported that US intelligence officials concluded a Chinese executive linked to a Singapore-based data centre company called Megaspeed had been funnelling information to Beijing. The executive, Alice Huang — also known as Huang Le, and no relation to 63-year-old Taiwanese-born Jensen — developed a close relationship with the Nvidia boss, the Times said. In a message to company employees released to media on Sunday, Huang acknowledged having an affair and apologised to his family and company staff. Nvidia is a global leader in producing chips used to train and run AI models and one of the world’s most valuable companies, and last year became the first to reach a market capitalisation of $5 trillion. Technology analyst Dan Ives, at the investment bank Yorkville Ives, said the crisis would at the very least spark congressional inquiries and “create an overhang on the stock for a myriad of reasons”. “This will add risk to the stock as he is so important to the Nvidia story and strategy globally,” Ives said. “This will also increase major scrutiny regarding selling chips to China, which remains a key battleground issue in DC,” he added. item.title: Nigeria loses 50% of farm produce to poor infrastructure – Alabi
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja ABUJA – Founder of Davidorlah Farms, Segun Alabi, has called on the National Assembly to increase funding for agriculture and prioritise investments in storage, transportation and processing infrastructure, warning that Nigeria loses between 45 and 50 per cent of its agricultural produce annually to post-harvest losses. Alabi said Nigeria’s food security challenges could not be addressed through increased production alone without adequate infrastructure to preserve, process and distribute farm produce. He argued that the huge volume of agricultural produce wasted annually represents lost revenue, employment opportunities and potential export earnings. The entrepreneur made the call while addressing journalists during activities marking the 10th anniversary of Davidorlah Farms, themed, “Davidorlah at 10: A Decade of Growth, A Future of Value Creation in Abuja.” He urged lawmakers to make agricultural infrastructure and value addition priorities in national economic planning, stressing that processing facilities located close to farming communities would reduce waste, create jobs and strengthen rural economies. “We don’t ask too much from the government. There is no company that can actually thrive without government intervention. What we ask for is to create an enabling environment where business can thrive and to improve infrastructure. Because agriculture without infrastructure would become a catastrophe,” he said. Alabi maintained that Nigeria’s major agricultural challenge was not necessarily inadequate primary production but the absence of facilities to preserve and process what farmers harvest. “The problem of Nigeria today is not an issue of primary production, but the issue of infrastructure. Every year, we lose more than 45 to 50 per cent of what we produce per annum. So, if you’re talking about food security, then more focus should be on infrastructure than primary production. If infrastructure is in place, there will be a reduction in post-harvest loss,” he said. He said establishing processing factories near agricultural production centres would enable farmers and businesses to convert raw commodities into commercially viable products for local consumption and international markets. The Davidorlah Farms founder also expressed the ambition to see Nigerian agricultural products gain wider acceptance in foreign markets through improved processing, packaging and quality standards. “I am looking for a time when you will leave Nigeria, get to America and Europe, and you will see products from Nigeria. My joy will be that when I’m on Qatar Airways or British Airways, I see produce from Nigeria that has been added value to it and it’s being sold in international markets. That is the dream,” he said. item.title: Mourinho wins La Liga Manager of the Month award after perfect October
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho has been named La Liga Manager of the Month for October after guiding the Spanish giants to three consecutive victories, including a 2-1 El Clasico triumph over Barcelona. La Liga announced the Portuguese coach as the October winner in a post on its official X account on Monday, recognising his side’s 100 per cent winning record in the league during the month. “Real Madrid’s coach is the Coach of the Month for October in #LALIGAEASPORTS,” the post read. Mourinho’s side began the month with a 1-0 victory over Villarreal before thrashing Sevilla 4-1 and defeating Barcelona 2-1 in their first El Clasico meeting of the season. The victory over Barcelona on October 25 was particularly significant, as it handed the Catalan side their first league defeat of the campaign after winning their opening nine matches. Kylian Mbappe scored twice for Madrid, while Raphinha got Barcelona’s only goal in the encounter. Mourinho emerged ahead of Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone and Real Sociedad coach Pellegrino Matarazzo, who were also nominated for the monthly award. Simeone guided Atletico to three victories during October, beating Alaves 2-1 before recording 1-0 wins over Espanyol and Deportivo La Coruna. Matarazzo also led Real Sociedad to three league wins, defeating Deportivo La Coruna 3-2, Malaga 5-2 and Levante 2-1. Despite their strong performances, Mourinho secured the recognition after Madrid’s perfect league record and victory over their arch-rivals. The award marks another milestone in the Portuguese manager’s return to the Santiago Bernabeu, where he previously coached from 2010 to 2013. During his first spell, Mourinho won the La Liga title, Copa del Rey and Spanish Super Cup. He succeeds Barcelona manager Hansi Flick, who won the September award. Madrid have also maintained a strong position in the title race, sitting second in the standings, three points behind Barcelona. They have suffered two league defeats this season, against Real Betis and Atletico Madrid. item.title: 2027: We’re looking up to God – Ebube Muonso
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu AWKA – The founder of Holy Ghost Adoration Ministry, Uke, Anambra State, Rev. Fr. Emmanuel Obimma, popularly known as Ebube Muonso, has expressed concern over the credibility and outcome of the 2027 general elections, saying Nigerians are looking up to God for divine intervention. The Catholic priest said the country needed a leader who would understand and address the suffering of ordinary Nigerians, lamenting what he described as the failure of political leaders to improve the country’s condition. Obimma spoke with journalists at Blessed Iwene Tansi Parish, Umudioka, Dunukofia Local Government Area of Anambra State. He said his closeness to ordinary Nigerians had given him an understanding of their economic difficulties and frustrations, unlike politicians who, according to him, were disconnected from the realities facing the masses. “I am close to the masses, unlike the politicians. I stand a better chance of telling the politicians the condition of the masses. Nigeria is finished; our politicians have destroyed this country. My prayer is that God will give us a leader after His heart to salvage the situation,” he said. The cleric, however, expressed concern about the prospects of the 2027 elections, arguing that defeating an incumbent could be difficult because of the advantages associated with occupying political office. “I know that next year’s election will not be easy, but with God all things are possible. It is very difficult to remove an incumbent because he has the security paraphernalia which are under his control and he also has access to the country’s finances. “Human beings may have all these, but God has the final say. That is our fate and confidence that God is still in control,” he said. Obimma urged Nigerians not to lose hope or become discouraged by concerns about the credibility of the electoral process. He said his interactions with citizens suggested growing disillusionment, with some expressing doubts that their votes would count even if their preferred candidates secured victory at the polls. The priest attributed the apprehension to the perception that the incumbent was an experienced politician capable of manipulating the electoral process, but maintained that Nigerians should still exercise their franchise. He urged eligible voters to come out and participate in the elections, insisting that political power remained subject to God’s ultimate authority. According to him, Nigerians already know the candidates they consider most qualified to lead the country towards greatness and should make their choices accordingly. item.title: 2027: SMBLF urges judiciary, INEC to act independently
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA – The Southern and Middle Belt Leaders Forum (SMBLF) has urged the judiciary and electoral institutions to act independently and expeditiously ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning that prolonged uncertainty over party leadership and candidates’ eligibility could deprive voters of meaningful choices. The forum also called on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to urgently conduct an independent forensic audit of the voters’ register following concerns over suspected artificial intelligence-generated photographs, duplicate entries and records allegedly belonging to unknown persons in the preliminary register published by the commission. The calls came amid growing political tension ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential and National Assembly elections. The forum’s position may be linked to the recent Federal High Court judgment in Abuja which nullified the leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) led by Senator David Mark and invalidated actions taken by the affected executives on behalf of the party. The development has raised questions about the party’s leadership and its preparations for the 2027 elections. The SMBLF also condemned reported attacks on political figures, including the presidential candidate of the Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, in Makurdi and Omoyele Sowore of the African Action Congress (AAC) in Ekiti State. It called on security agencies to investigate the incidents, identify those responsible and prosecute offenders where evidence establishes culpability. The forum made its position known in a statement issued on Monday and jointly signed by its Chairman and leader of Afenifere, Oba Oladipo Olaitan; President-General of Ohanaeze Ndigbo Worldwide, Senator John Azuta-Mbata; National Chairman of the Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF), Ambassador Godknows Igali; and President of the Middle Belt Forum, Dr Bitrus Pogu. The leaders expressed concern over what they described as an increasingly tense political atmosphere, warning that the country could not afford an electoral process undermined by doubts about institutional integrity, intimidation of political opponents and uncertainty over citizens’ democratic choices. “Our most urgent concern is the disturbing discovery of suspected Artificial Intelligence (AI)-generated photographs, duplicate entries and records reportedly belonging to unknown persons in the preliminary voters’ register published by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). “These revelations followed public release of registration data and have provoked widespread anxiety about the credibility of the forthcoming polls,” the statement said. The forum demanded an urgent forensic audit involving electoral technology specialists, civil society representatives and other qualified stakeholders to establish the authenticity and integrity of the register. item.title: Brighton’s Yohanna makes Chelle’s 23-man list for DR Congo clash
item.description: Brighton forward Zadok Yohanna and Molde FC midfielder Daniel Daga have been named in Nigeria’s 23-man squad for the 2028 Olympic Games football qualifiers against the Democratic Republic of Congo. Head coach Èric Chelle included the duo among the foreign-based players selected for the two-legged second-round qualifying tie as the Olympic Eagles seek a place at next year’s U-23 Africa Cup of Nations in Egypt. The tournament will also determine Africa’s representatives at the men’s football event of the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles. Goalkeeper Michael Atata, who has received several invitations to the senior national team, is also included alongside SJK FC’s Samuel James and Rivers United’s Clinton Andy. Other notable names in the squad include Genk defender Christian Akpan, FC Basel’s Victory Akpe, Tromsø defender Vince Osuji, Fulham midfielder Chibuzor Nwoko and Benfica forward Peter Edokpolor. Seven players from the Nigeria Premier Football League are also included in the squad. The first leg will take place at Stade TP Mazembe in Lubumbashi on Friday, November 13, while the return fixture is scheduled for November 17 at the Remo Stars Stadium in Ikenne-Remo. Nigeria received a bye in the first qualifying round and must overcome DR Congo over two legs to advance to the final qualifying round. Meanwhile, assistant coach Deniran Ortega will lead the Olympic Eagles against DR Congo in Chelle’s absence as the Franco- Malian coach focuses on the Super Eagles’ 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying double-header against Tanzania. Ortega, who has worked with the U-23 players since the team’s camp opened two weeks ago, will be assisted by Ikorodu City head coach Bright Ozebagbe. The scheduling conflict means Chelle will oversee the senior team during the same international window in which the Olympic Eagles play their qualifying fixtures. Nigeria’s full 23-man squad: Goalkeepers: Samuel James (SJK FC, Finland), Clinton Andy (Rivers United), Michael Atata (Ikorodu City). Defenders: Christian Akpan (Genk FC, Belgium), Victory Akpe (FC Basel, Switzerland), Vince Osuji (Tromsø IL, Norway), Emmanuel Godwin (Pardubice FC, Czechia), Odinaka Alfred (Nasarawa United), Emmanuel Ochobi (Rivers United), Aliu Sugau (Barau FC). Midfielders: John Otomewo (Reims FC, France), Daniel Daga (Molde FC, Norway), Wilfred George (Kristiansund FC, Norway), Chibuzor Nwoko (Fulham FC, England), Aderemi Adeoye (Ikorodu City), Sadiq Saleh (FC Metta, Latvia), Victor Samuel (Pardubice FC, Czechia). Forwards: Peter Edokpolor (SL Benfica, Portugal), Sulaiman Sani (Al-Qadsiah FC, Saudi Arabia), Umar Abubakar (FC Famalicao, Portugal), Zadok Yohanna (Brighton FC, England), Abdullahi Umar (Hradec Kralove, Czechia), Abdulmuiz Adeleke (Sporting Supreme). item.title: Yari never called Nigerian youths lazy – Group insists
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The Senator Yari National Unity Project for Tinubu 2027 has dismissed reports that Senator Abdul’aziz Abubakar Yari described Nigerian youths as lazy, accusing sections of the media of misrepresenting his remarks at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State. The group said Yari, Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, was speaking about hunger, food availability and the dignity of hard work, rather than disparaging young Nigerians. In a statement issued by its National Coordinator, Dr Sani Abdullahi Shinkafi, the group challenged those circulating the allegation to watch the full footage of Yari’s address, insisting that the senator had acknowledged the economic hardship facing Nigerians before making his remarks on productivity. “He opened his remark by stating plainly: ‘We have hunger.’ At no point in that remark did the Senator mention, single out or describe Nigerian youths. To turn a statement on the dignity of work, made by a man who had just acknowledged that hunger exists, into the headline ‘Yari calls youths lazy’ is not reporting; it is spin,” the statement said. To support its position, the group cited Yari’s interventions in education, military recruitment, agriculture and public-sector employment, arguing that his record demonstrated his commitment to the welfare and empowerment of young Nigerians. It also claimed that Yari facilitated the enlistment of 158 young people from Zamfara West into two Nigerian Army recruitment intakes and supported farmers with agricultural inputs and equipment. “A leader who sends thousands of young people to university and into national service does not hold Nigerian youths in contempt; he invests in them,” the statement added. The group reaffirmed its confidence in Yari and directed its officers nationwide to intensify grassroots mobilisation for President Bola Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election. It also urged media organisations that published the disputed report to review the full footage of the senator’s address and correct what it described as a misrepresentation. “Political disagreement is legitimate; misrepresentation is not,” the statement added. item.title: 2027: Any Igbo against Obi is enemy of Ndigbo – Victor Umeh
item.description: Senator Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central Senatorial District, has declared that any Igbo person opposed to the presidential ambition of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate, Peter Obi, is an enemy of Ndigbo. Umeh, who described Obi as the conscience of the Igbo people, also cautioned political leaders in the South-East, particularly the Anambra State Government, against working against the former governor’s presidential ambition ahead of the 2027 general elections. The senator, popularly known as Ohamadike, made the remarks in a trending video, on Monday. He said Obi represented the collective aspirations of the Igbo people and urged the people of the South-East to rally behind him. “I’m an Igbo activist, you people know me and you hear my voice in the Senate on all issues of national importance. Peter is our conscience in this election. Any Igbo man who stands up to say we will not vote for Peter Obi, I’m telling you that he’s an enemy of Igbo people,” Umeh said. He specifically warned the Anambra State Government against allegedly opposing Obi’s ambition for political reasons, arguing that the state’s leadership should consider the broader interests of the Igbo people. Umeh claimed he played a significant role in the emergence of Governor Chukwuma Soludo, insisting that the office of governor was held in trust for the collective interest of the people. “This government in the state, I helped installing it. Nobody came here the governor of Anambra State since 2003 without my input. This one that is serving, I was a principal contributor to his ascending to that office. He’s holding that office on trust for all of us,” he said. The senator urged Soludo not to undermine Obi’s presidential ambition, describing any attempt to work against his kinsman as an abomination. “Let him not commit what is called abomination by wanting to destroy his brother in the name of politics,” he warned. Umeh further argued that if politicians from other geopolitical zones were free to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu, Igbo people should equally be allowed to rally behind Obi without intimidation or condemnation. Recalling Obi’s support for him, the senator called on Ndigbo to stand for what he described as truth and justice, adding that Obi’s success in the 2027 presidential election would be a collective achievement for the South-East. “He told me this is his time and if he makes it, the Igbos have made it. item.title: FG considers assessment tests for Nigerians with foreign degrees before NYSC
item.description: The Federal Government is considering the introduction of assessment test for Nigerians who obtain degrees from foreign institutions, particularly in African countries. Dr Folake Olatunji-David, Acting Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Education, disclosed this at the 37th meeting of the National Standing Committee (NSC) on Evaluation of Foreign Qualifications in Abuja on Monday. Olatunji-David said the assessment test was necessary before their qualifications would be evaluated for mobilisation into the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC). She said the proposal was aimed at ensuring that foreign qualifications presented by Nigerians reflected genuine learning achievements and met the required academic standards. She explained that the measure was particularly important given the increasing number of Nigerians studying in foreign higher institutions, especially in West Africa. “We must ensure that the standard of education in Nigeria is not lowered by allowing all manner of foreign qualifications that are not recognised to be paraded by Nigerians without the corresponding learning achievement. “In as much as we want to encourage global socialisation, education, and the rest of them because the world is a global village now, but we want to maintain standard. “We want to ensure that, yes, for every certificate given, they are earned, and they can produce people that can contribute positively to our national development. “I therefore invite this committee once again to consider, if necessary, an assessment test before such graduates are evaluated for NYSC,” she said. Olatunji-David described the committee as central to efforts to safeguard the integrity of Nigeria’s education system by ensuring that only genuine and duly accredited foreign qualifications were recognised. She expressed concern over the rising cases of forgery of Nigerian and foreign degree certificates, saying the ministry was taking steps to address the menace. The acting permanent secretary commended members of the committee for decisions reached at their previous meeting, describing them as important steps towards improving the evaluation and accreditation of foreign qualifications. She said the ministry had recorded progress in confirming the accreditation status of foreign institutions, issuing clearance letters for NYSC mobilisation, authenticating certificates and issuing no-objection letters. According to her, the ministry also issues eligibility and proficiency letters to Nigerians travelling abroad for employment or further studies. “Since the beginning of this year, the evaluation of foreign certificates and authentication of Nigerian certificates have been automated and digitalised, making the process seamless. “The fees accruing are remitted into government accounts, thereby increasing the ministry’s revenue generation,” Olatunji-David said. item.title: Youth Olympics: Nwankwo, Bright Win Historic Gold In Men’s, Women’s 100m
item.description: Nigeria made an impressive start to the athletics competition at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games on Sunday, winning gold in both the men’s and women’s 100m finals at the Complexe Iba Mar Diop. Rosemary Nwankwo opened the country’s gold-medal account in the women’s 100m, crossing the finish line in 11.16 seconds to claim victory and set a new personal best. Nigeria’s Rosemary Nwankwo, gold medalist (C), Arwa Ali of the United Arab Emirates (L), silver medalist, and Dana Salem of Qatar (R), bronze medalist, pose on the podium after the women’s 100-meter track and field final at the 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games, held at the Iba Mar Diop Complex (CID Stadium) in Dakar on November 8, 2026. (Photo by NICOLAS REMENE / AFP) She finished ahead of Arwa Ali of the United Arab Emirates, who clocked 11.41 seconds, also a personal best, while Dana Salem of Qatar settled for bronze in 11.48 seconds. The win made Nwankwo the third Nigerian woman to take Youth Olympic 100m gold, following Josephine Omaka at the inaugural Singapore 2010 Games and Rosemary Chukwuma at Buenos Aires 2018. Nigeria’s Rosemary Nwankwo, winner of the women’s 100-meter track and field final at the 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games, poses next to the board at the Iba Mar Diop Complex (CID Stadium) in Dakar on November 8, 2026. (Photo by NICOLAS REMENE / AFP) Nigeria’s celebrations continued minutes later as Gift Bright secured another gold medal in the men’s 100m, finishing in a personal-best time of 10.28 seconds. China’s Zhang Hangyu came second in 10.57 seconds, while Poland’s Szymon Dolega claimed bronze in 10.61 seconds. Speaking after her triumph, Nwankwo said she remained focused on her race despite the significance of the occasion. Nigeria’s Gift Bright, react after winning the men’s 100-meter semifinal at the 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games, held at the Iba Mar Diop Complex (CID Stadium) in Dakar on November 8, 2026. (Photo by NICOLAS REMENE / AFP) “There was no pressure on me. I run my race. I focused on me, and I did it,” she said. “I’ve prayed for this moment, and I did it.” For Bright, the victory was particularly significant after a thigh injury had troubled him in the two weeks leading up to the competition. China’s Hangyu Zhang (L), silver medalist; Nigeria’s Gift Bright (C), gold medalist; and Poland’s Szymon Dolega (R), bronze medalist, pose on the podium after the men’s 100-meter track and field final at the 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games, held at the Iba Mar Diop Complex (CID Stadium) in Dakar on November 8, 2026. (Photo by NICOLAS REMENE / AFP) He admitted that the injury had affected his confidence but said he was relieved to compete without pain in the final. “I want to tell you guys that at the next (Youth) Olympics, expect Nigeria to win it again. We are good sprinters,” he said. We know how to condition ourselves to stay where we are. It’s a very big thing for us.” The post Youth Olympics: Nwankwo, Bright Win Historic Gold In Men’s, Women’s 100m appeared first on

item.title: Obi Alleges NFF Blocked Him From Greeting Victorious Flamingos
item.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate Peter Obi has alleged that officials of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) prevented him from greeting members of the national Under-17 women’s football team, the Flamingos, following their historic victory at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Obi said he was allegedly informed that the officials had warned against allowing him to approach the players, allegedly threatening that they would lose their jobs if he did. The former Anambra State governor disclosed this in a statement posted on his official X handle on Monday, after the Flamingos returned to Nigeria following their 2-1 victory over Japan in Saturday’s final in Morocco. Obi said he arrived at the airport at about 7 a.m. on Monday to board a flight to Enugu when he sighted the victorious team preparing to leave the airport. Flamingos arriving in Nigeria. He said he subsequently asked his protocol officer, Jackie Wayas, to find out whether he could greet and welcome the players. “With genuine joy and enthusiasm, I asked my Protocol Officer, Jackie Wayas, to find out whether I could greet and welcome the team. I was informed that officials of the Nigerian Football Federation (NFF) had refused and had requested that I not approach them because, if I did, they would all lose their jobs,” he wrote. Obi described the incident as another example of what he called the growing culture of “toxic politics” in Nigeria, alleging that he had experienced similar treatment during a previous visit to a football event. He recounted that on March 25, 2025, he travelled to Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, for a World Cup qualifying match, where he said the governor received him at the VIP stand. According to him, after the match, other government officials were allowed to greet the players, but he was again prevented from doing so. “Following the match, other government officials went to greet the players, but I was again prevented from doing so. I was told by the officials that they would lose their jobs if I proceeded,” he said. The former governor expressed concern over what he described as the increasing politicisation of public engagements, arguing that political differences should not prevent Nigerians from celebrating national achievements. “It is deeply troubling to witness the extent of toxic politics into which our nation has descended since 2025. Each year appears to bring further deterioration. This reflects how deeply Nigeria has been affected. “The new Nigeria we aspire to build must have no room for hostility, intimidation, or discrimination, regardless of political affiliation. It must be a Nigeria in which unity, mutual respect, and our shared humanity take,” he said. item.title: PFIPC Scandal: FG Files Fresh Amended Charges Against Adeyemi Adeniyi, Four Others
item.description: The Federal Government has filed a fresh 36-count amended charge against the embattled Director-General of the Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council (PFIPC), Adeyemi Adeniyi, and four others over alleged forgery, false representation and fraud. Adeniyi appeared alongside his co-defendants before Justice Halilu Yusuf of the Federal Capital Territory High Court in Maitama, Abuja, on Monday. However, their arraignment on the fresh charges could not proceed due to the absence of the fourth defendant, Florence Omemah, who was reportedly ill. Prosecution counsel, Sylvanus Tahir, informed the court that Ms Omemah was receiving treatment at a hospital in Abuja. He subsequently requested a seven-day adjournment to enable her to recover and appear in court to take her plea. Counsel to Mr Adeniyi, Ibrahim Angulu, however, urged the court to grant a shorter adjournment to allow him to pursue bail for his client. He also told the court that Mr Adeniyi had been in detention for more than 200 days. In a brief ruling, Justice Yusuf adjourned the case until November 18 for the arraignment of all the defendants. The judge further ordered that Mr Adeniyi be remanded at the Kuje Correctional Centre, while the other defendants should remain in the custody of the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC). Alleged Fake Government Agency Adeniyi Adeyemi paraded himself as the DG of the PFIPC. Photo: X@BayoOnanuga. The case centres on allegations that Adeniyi established a fictitious federal agency known as the Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council and falsely presented himself as its director-general. Investigators alleged that the agency had no legal backing and that Mr Adeniyi forged appointment letters and signatures attributed to the Chief of Staff to the President to legitimise his purported position. According to investigators, he occupied offices previously used by the defunct Presidential Economic Advisory Council at the Federal Secretariat in Abuja and allegedly held unauthorised meetings with foreign diplomats. He was also accused of seeking official visa documentation for United States visas and operating 34 bank accounts. Investigators further alleged that he exploited loopholes in the civil service system to secure a proposed allocation of ₦1.302 billion for the fictitious agency in the 2026 budget. ICPC Uncovers Other Alleged Fake Agencies Following an interim report presented to President Bola Tinubu, the ICPC reportedly uncovered two other allegedly fictitious agencies linked to Mr Adeniyi: the FCT Investment Promotion Agency and the Foreign Investment Promotion Agency. The commission also recommended disciplinary action against some public officials suspected of assisting the alleged scheme. In October 2026, the Federal High Court in Abuja struck out the initial eight-count charge after jurisdictional concerns prompted the Attorney-General of the Federation to withdraw the case.
